review.reason: Candidate 8 works as a publishable three-hole set, and the generated artwork can be mapped confidently left-to-right to holes 1, 2, and 3. Hole 1 is the dry 219-yard punchbowl par 3; the illustration keeps the no-water look, the broad receiving area, and the left-side bunkering around the green/approach. Hole 2 is the 498-yard reachable par 5 with one substantial fairway-side lake on the right; the art preserves the playable left landing corridor and the long water hazard, which supports a clear layup-versus-aggressive second-shot choice. Hole 3 is the 370-yard cape par 4 with water left/front and bunkering right of the green; the illustration matches that overall shape and side balance well enough. Across the round, the sequence has strong variety: one-shot punchbowl, reachable par 5 with right-side water, then a shorter cape par 4 with left-side water. Difficulty is assertive but fair because each water hole still leaves a credible safer route, and the dry par 3 gives the set a breather without becoming bland. I do not see a clear, safe geometry change that is needed to reconcile the artwork: water counts and hazard sides remain consistent with the authoritative geometry, and there is no obvious bunker-side mismatch severe enough to justify an edit.
